note: claude-opus-5-5、入力 3110 / 出力 2091 トークン

data.interpretation: The KPI has three parts. (1) Maximize the number of orders delivered within the promised times, town-wide. This is the primary objective and maps to on_time_deliveries; with the same seed and order stream it is equivalent to on_time_rate. (2) 'Leave no company's customers behind' is a fairness condition across companies, but it can be measured in several ways. (3) Regulation revisions (constitution invariants and quorum) may be proposed when votes or the constitution block customer-beneficial amendments. Each proposal must state who is affected and how. Part 3 is a process rule, not a measurable target: any such proposal goes to the human with an impact statement covering companies A, B, C and the customers. The KPI states no numeric levels, so no targets or guard values are set.

options.label: Town-wide on-time count, protecting the worst-off company's on-time rate

goals.text: Maximize the number of orders delivered within the promised time across the town.
Monitor the on-time rate of the worst-off company so that no company's customers fall behind.
Monitor orders left undelivered at period end, so that hard-to-serve orders are not abandoned to raise the on-time count.
Monitor the worst company's 95th-percentile wait, so that one company's customers do not suffer long waits.

options.note: Recommended. Total on-time deliveries drive improvement. Fairness is read as raising the floor, not narrowing the gap, so it cannot be 'improved' by making the best company worse. No levels are set because the KPI gives none.

options.label: Town-wide on-time count, keeping companies' on-time rates close together

goals.text: Maximize the number of orders delivered within the promised time across the town.
Monitor the gap between the best and worst company on-time rates, so that no company's customers fall behind the others.
Monitor orders left undelivered at period end.

options.note: Reads 'leave no one behind' as equality between companies. A gap metric can shrink when the best company gets worse, so it can look fair while customers are worse off overall.

options.label: Worst-off company first (maximin), with town-wide on-time count monitored

goals.text: Maximize the on-time rate of the worst-off company.
Monitor the town-wide number of on-time deliveries so the total does not drop.
Monitor orders left undelivered at period end.

options.note: Treats 'leave no company behind' as the primary aim. This can reject amendments that greatly raise total on-time deliveries but leave the weakest company unchanged.

concerns: 'Leave no company's customers behind' can mean raising the worst company's on-time rate, narrowing the gap between companies, or limiting the worst company's long waits. These readings can rank amendments differently.

Total on-time deliveries and the worst company's on-time rate can conflict. An amendment may raise the town total while lowering one company's rate. The KPI does not say which wins, or by how much a company may fall.
on_time_deliveries is a proxy that ignores orders that are already late. Optimizing it alone can deprioritize late or difficult orders and leave them unfinished. This is why unfinished is monitored.

The KPI states no numeric levels (e.g., a minimum per-company on-time rate). So no targets or guards are set, and only worsening of the monitored goals is watched. Please state levels if hard limits are wanted.

Regulation revisions (constitution invariants, quorum) cannot be judged by metrics. They will always be sent to you for decision, with a statement of the effects on companies A, B, C and on customers. In particular, lowering the quorum removes companies' ability to block changes that hurt them, and relaxing invariants can weaken road safety or customer protections.
